- Ironvale Athletic increased press from 0.22 to 0.4 and directness from 0.66 to 0.81 at 82' to chase the game [#1477].
- After the tactical change, Ironvale's xG rose from 0 to 0.6 and shots from 0 to 5 in 12 minutes [#1477].
- Possession stayed almost the same for Ironvale (55.9% before, 55.8% after) but field tilt increased from 5.9% to 65.2% [#1477].
- Opponent xG dropped sharply from 1.57 to 0.03 following Ironvale's tactical shift [#1477].
- Score remained Redmond Rovers 3, Ironvale Athletic 2 after the change [#1477].

- Ironvale Athletic, initially set up in a 5-3-2 formation with a low block, deep defensive line, and a focus on direct, vertical passing, shifted tactics at 82 minutes to press higher and play more direct, increasing press intensity from 0.22 to 0.4, directness from 0.66 to 0.81, and line height from 0.25 to 0.37 [#1477].  
- This tactical change aimed to break Redmond Rovers’ dominance in field position and chances, reflected in Ironvale’s field tilt rising sharply from 5.9% to 65.2% and shots increasing from 0 to 5 in the 12 minutes following the change, indicating a more aggressive, forward pattern likely focused on press-induced turnovers and quick transitions [#1477].  
- The shift to a higher press and more direct play contrasted with Redmond’s 4-3-3 style of high press, quick circulation, and high defensive line, forcing Ironvale to abandon their typical deep, counter-attacking approach in favor of an offensive overload or pressing trap to claw back possession and create opportunities [#1477].  
- Despite the increased aggression, Ironvale’s pressing led to a slight rise in high turnovers (from 1 to 2) and a nearly stable possession percentage (~56%), suggesting that while their intent was to disrupt Redmond’s control patterns, they risked exposure to counter-attacks from the home side’s structure [#1477].
